text:
Ethan: quick post-all-hands question about offsite approvals and travel policy wording. wanted to make sure managers don't get mixed signals when approving cross-team offsites.

Priya: good call. what specifically is confusing?

Ethan: all-hands said "6 weeks notice" but some teams were told 4 weeks by facilities. which is correct for medium-size offsites (~30 ppl)?

Maya: facilities updated the short-lead process last month. TL;DR: standard is 6 weeks for budgeted offsites. for "short-lead" internal-only gatherings under 25 people we can accept 4 weeks if no external vendors. I'll paste the short rule below.

Maya: ```Short-lead exception (internal <25): submit via People Ops form -> facilities triage -> approval within 5 business days. No external vendors. No travel reimbursements without prior sign-off.```

Ethan: great. also manager asked about travel booking for mixed itineraries (customer + conference). do we use combined cost for approval thresholds?

Priya: yes combine total estimated cost. if part of the trip is billed to a customer partner, note the split in the request and attach the customer PO if available.

Leo: ops note: we tightened per-diem rules for international travel last quarter. people asked about meals for overnight training days  if training is company-mandated, meals are reimbursable under per-diem; if optional, only travel days are covered.

ops-bot: New doc published: "Hybrid & Offsite Playbook v3" https://intranet.redwood/ops/hybrid-offsite-playbook-v3 (auto) :page_facing_up:

Ethan: lovely. one last ask  can People Ops put a one-line in the manager digest clarifying short-lead exception and combined-cost rule? managers are the gatekeepers.

Priya: yes, will include in Tuesday digest and drop a manager-friendly checklist.

Ethan: thanks everyone, I'll close the loop with eng leads after the digest posts. :white_check_mark:
